# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-8 (Extended v86)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Winter Year 2, approximately late 1825-1826)**: Valjean and Cosette in sanctuary at Convent of Petit-Picpus during a nun's death and funeral arrangements. Key dates: 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, Valjean's theft and flight; Waterloo/Hougomont June 17-18); 1817 (young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral tenure); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest; Javert's revelation; TRIAL SEQUENCE in Arras; Valjean's self-revelation; acquittal of Champmathieu; RETURN TO M. SUR M. before six a.m.; Fantine's death; Valjean arrested beside death-bed; VALJEAN ESCAPES same evening)**; December 1823 (Montfermeil rescue of Cosette, 1,500-franc payment to Thénardier); **December 26, 1823 (Valjean and Cosette returned to Paris via Barrier Monceaux)**; 1824 spring onward (decrepit building lodging; winter passed; spring advanced); **Summer Year 2**: Achieved sanctuary inside walled garden compound, le Petit-Picpus district. **Winter Year 2 (Current)**: A nun (Mother Crucifixion) dying at daybreak; community occupied with prayers of forty hours and funeral arrangements.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles); **English harbor towns** (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Ravenmere, Staveford, Ostcombe, Gulhaven): Luvie reading almanac; Luvie giving sealed letter to Wilwick via eldest son of Vesmira Thornmere; Gadrek Prydenridge laughing; river up in spring; Isric falling asleep; Jotho discussing oats prices with carter; wife of Tatho Brackick planning trip to Elmhaven but staying; light going early; frost silvering hedges; wind from water with salt and tar smell; children chasing hoop shrieking; rain threatening but holding off; gulls quarreling over fish heads by steps. Arras; Waterloo; Toulon; Paris districts including Mouffetard quarter. **Gorbeau House** (Rue de la Cosette area, Mouffetard): Decrepit lodging where Valjean and Cosette previously lodged; old woman portress; Javert's surveillance station. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, unpaved roads; roads all ruts and puddles after thaw. **Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (CONVENT CARRIAGE GATE)**: Ajar gate, courtyard, vine-hung walls, tall trees above wall. **Wall (approximately 18 feet)**: Extends from niche to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur. **CONVENT COMPLEX - THREE BUILDINGS**: (1) **Great Convent**: Inhabited by Bernardines-Benedictines nuns; gloomy building, heavily shuttered window with sheet zinc. (2) **Boarding-school**: Where scholars lodged. (3) **Little Convent**: Building with garden housing aged nuns of various orders destroyed in Revolution. **INTERIOR GARDEN (Great Convent)**: Vast oblong area; alley of large poplars; forest trees in corners; solitary gnarled tree, fruit-trees, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well, stone benches, grass and green mould. **PARLOR (Great Convent)**: Monstrous lattice of iron bars (squares less than 1.5 inches diagonal) riveted by clenched-fist fastenings; behind lattice: barrier of black shutters reinforced with gingerbread-yellow wooden beams, always closed; behind shutters: nun's voice screened by iron grating and plate with thousand holes; slat opens revealing nun's mouth and chin only, covered with black veil, guimpe, shroud. **BURIAL LOCATIONS**: Lower hall of church communicates with street, no men enter except doctor of dead; **Vaugirard cemetery**: Ancient cemetery outside regulations, going to be suppressed, has special Permission from Prefecture for nuns to be taken there at nightfall.

## Convent of the Bernardines of the Perpetual Adoration
[Same as before—order lineage, dress, austerity, vows, operational rules, reparation practice, possessions rule, hourly bells, chanting, men allowed]

**CURRENT DEATH AND FUNERAL ARRANGEMENTS**: **Mother Crucifixion died at daybreak** (Winter Year 2, current time). She retained consciousness to last moment, spoke to community then to angels, gave final commands. Prioress (Mother Innocente/Mademoiselle de Blemeur) describes her death as "precious"—she smiled, community felt she was regaining life in God, something of paradise in her death. **FUNERAL PROCEDURE ESTABLISHED**: Sisters will lay out body; Fauchelevent will close coffin; sisters carry coffin to chapel; office for dead said; community returns to cloister. **BETWEEN 11 P.M. AND MIDNIGHT**: Fauchelevent to come with iron bar (lever) to vault. Mother Precentors and Mother Ascension present. Vault opened, coffin lowered into vault (beneath grand altar—government forbids coffin burial but nuns have special privilege via Prefecture Permission for nighttime Vaugirard cemetery burials). Vault closed again. No trace, government has no suspicion. Doctor has already signed death passport, undertaker company will bring empty coffin, undertaker's men collect it. **FAUCHELEVENT'S UNDERSTANDING**: Nuns don't count undertaker's men or himself as "men" entering burial hall; a gardener is "a bit of a grave-digger"; burial is box fetched empty, taken away with something in it. Friend Father Mestienne is grave-digger at Vaugirard cemetery.

## Prioress and Vocal Mothers (1819-1825 Period, Confirmed)
**Mademoiselle de Blemeur (Mother Innocente)** (Prioress, 1819-1825): Age ~sixty; short, thick; "singing like a cracked pot"; excellent woman; only merry one in convent; learned, erudite, wise; proficient in history; descended from Marguerite de Blemeur, author of _Lives of the Saints of the Order of Saint-Benoît_; re-elected. **CURRENT OBSERVATION**: Ordinarily cheerful; upon entering, double form of preoccupation (grave and agitated air on critical occasions) imprinted on her countenance. Subject to barrier of silence with overfull reservoir; on day of death arrangements, rose and exclaimed with loquacity of dam breaking away, speaking extensively about Mother Crucifixion's death and spiritual merit. **Vocal Mothers**: Mother Sainte-Honorine; Mother Sainte-Gertrude (treasurer); Mother-Saint-Ange; Mother Annonciation (sacristan); Mother Saint-Augustin (nurse; only malicious one); Mother Sainte-Mechtilde (directs singing); Mother des Anges; Mother Saint-Joseph; Mother Sainte-Adélaide; Mother Miséricorde; Mother Compassion; Mother Providence; **Mother Présentation (future prioress 1847)**; Mother Sainte-Céligne; Mother Sainte-Chantal; **Mother Crucifixion (deceased, Winter Year 2)**; **Four Mother Precentors** (to be present at vault opening); **Mother Ascension** (to be present at vault opening).

## Jean Valjean's Sanctuary and Strategic Crisis
**CURRENT CRISIS**: Upon learning nun died and funeral procedures commencing, Valjean confronted with immediate danger: body must be removed from convent; convent doors opening; police still swarming streets. **VALJEAN'S TERROR**: Turned pale; very thought of descending again into "terrible street" made him shudder. Pictured entire police force engaged in swarming quarter, agents on watch, sentinels everywhere, "frightful fists extended towards his collar, Javert at the corner of the intersection of the streets perhaps." **PSYCHOLOGICAL STATE**: Altered appearance reflects sadness, uneasiness, anxiety, depression; continual tremor so long as Cosette near, needs nothing except her, fears nothing except her. **COSETTE'S STATUS**: Still sleeping; completely dependent on Valjean.

## Fauchelevent's Crucial Role and New Plan
**Identity**: Old crippled gardener; admitted approximately two years previously (1821) on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. **Current Situation**: Witnessed nun's death; heard bells ringing vocal mothers to chapter; understands funeral procedures and vault burial. **ESCAPE PLAN FOR COSETTE**: (1) Will use service door opening on courtyard; knock, porter opens; Cosette placed in vintage basket on his back, covered, appears natural—"Father Fauchelevent goes out with his basket—that is perfectly natural"; (2) Leave Cosette with deaf fruit-seller in Rue Chemin-Vert (good old friend) who has little bed; will shout in fruit-seller's ear that child is his niece, to keep her until tomorrow; (3) Cosette will re-enter with Valjean next day when Fauchelevent arranges it. **PLAN FOR VALJEAN**: Fauchelevent asked directly—"how will you manage to get out?" (awaiting Valjean's answer/plan; Fauchelevent will contrive to have him re-enter but method unclear). **CHARACTER**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; speaks freely; peasant of Picardy. **COMMITMENT AFFIRMED**: Perceived generous action as dying man perceives glass of good wine; old egoist finding sweetness in gratitude toward end of days. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; renders good action absolutely necessary to him; enlisted self-devotion, good will, old rustic cunning in enterprise. **STATUS**: Valjean's only known ally and protector in Paris; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's presence. **OPPORTUNITY**: Current funeral commotion and vault procedures (Mother Precentors, Mother Ascension present 11 p.m. to midnight) provides cover for movements.

## Javert's Pursuit and Ongoing Investigation (Unchanged)
**REASSIGNMENT TO PARIS** (January 1823): When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail, Javert attached to Paris police force. **NEWSPAPER REPORT** (December 1823): Newspaper announced Valjean's death; Javert remarked "That's a good entry." **REACTIVATION**: Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived Javert's memory; suspected Valjean had sought daughter. **JAVERT'S SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence. **REASONS FOR SECRECY**: (1) Slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead was magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen. **PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; at night Javert waited behind trees with two men. **ESCAPE FROM MOUFFETARD**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder in lantern, led astray. **STRATEGIC PURSUIT**: Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily (considered it risky, preferred gloating anticipation). **STATUS**: Even when saw Valjean escaped, sure convict could not be far off; established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades. Free press embarrassed police; arbitrary arrests denounced by newspapers; police agents afraid of mistakes.
